title: Mode 3 cost-engineering measures static line-count as a token proxy, not actual cost or wall-clock. Today's busy session produced 0 PROPs because the instrument is blind to actual per-run cost variance. Design real measurement.
context:
Operator-side observation 2026-06-14T09:20Z. Today included an operator-driven OBE audit + PROP-100/096-C1/098 implementation + DIRECTIVE-20260614-001 root-cause work — visibly heavy session. Tinker's 2026-06-14T08-41 Mode 3 run wrote `proposals_written: []` and called it clean, because:

(1) The cost_engineering instrument only measures `context_load` (per-agent total prompt + reference file line counts via `wc -l`), with a >10% growth alert threshold. This is a static proxy for per-run token cost — it assumes (cost ≈ static_load × runs_per_day) which is a coarse approximation that misses high-variance failure modes.

(2) No measurement of actual per-run input/output tokens. The scheduled-tasks MCP (`list_scheduled_tasks`) exposes only metadata (id, schedule, lastRunAt/nextRunAt). Per-run cost data lives in the Claude session JSONL transcripts (`/sessions/<session>/mnt/.claude/projects/<proj>/<run-id>.jsonl` for operator runs; scheduled-agent transcripts at an as-yet-unmapped path). Each assistant message in the JSONL has `usage.input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_creation_input_tokens`, `cache_read_input_tokens` — the raw material for true cost per run.

(3) No wall-clock duration measurement. Tinker's only timing signal today was 'agents producing within ~1-2h' — that's timestamp liveness for the dispatcher liveness check, not per-run duration.

(4) No variance tracking. A decider run during a directive storm reads 20 PROP files; one during a quiet hour reads 2. Static line-count can't see the difference. P95 cost vs median cost variance would catch unbounded loops (e.g., a Mode 3 walk that loads 100 PROP files for a context-load re-baseline).

(5) The standing-candidates list (decider dispatcher-split 4153L, workspace-sync further script-extraction 1585L) has been carried across multiple Mode 3 reports without triggering a new PROP, because line-count alone doesn't justify the high-cost design work — there's no real-cost signal saying 'decider runs cost $X today and the dispatcher-split would save $Y'.

Other-side check (operator already considered):
- Static line-count IS defensible IF prompts are stable across runs. It correctly catches prompt-drift (a separate failure mode from per-run variance).
- Adding measurement adds tinker run cost. If the data isn't actionable, it's net-negative.
- The biggest blind spot is operator-Claude session cost (today's OBE audit), which is OUT OF SCOPE for scheduled-agent instrumentation. Phase 2 problem.
- Per-run JSONL access requires tinker to know its own filesystem path to the transcripts. Validate this access path is reliable from tinker's run context (which is a separate scheduled-tasks session, not the operator's session) BEFORE building the measurement on it.

Key assertion from tinker's 08-41 report: 'no new PROP authored this run — the directive backlog cleared by the 07-54/08-21 runs plus a healthy pipeline meant the highest-value action was the overdue context-load re-baseline + re-work audit rather than a speculative new optimization PROP.' This is a defensible judgment FROM A WALKER THAT CANNOT SEE ACTUAL COSTS. The fix is to make it see costs, then re-evaluate.
task: Design Mode 3 instrumentation upgrade that measures actual per-run cost (input × output tokens × model pricing), wall-clock duration, and cross-run variance — not just static prompt line-counts. Author as PROP-NNN with phased rollout.
investigation_questions: Q1 — Access path. Can tinker's scheduled-agent run actually read JSONL transcripts for other scheduled agents? Map the path. Hypotheses: (a) tinker's session has access to `/sessions/<its-session>/mnt/.claude/projects/...` but NOT other agents' sessions; (b) each scheduled agent's transcripts live under its own session ID with no shared mount; (c) there's a shared log path tinker doesn't currently read. Probe by listing what tinker can `ls` from its scheduled-task runtime. If JSONL access is not available, the fallback is to instrument each agent to self-report its own usage at end-of-run by writing it to its existing report file (decider/analyst/curmudgeon/etc already write `monitor/<agent>/report-*.json` — add a `usage` field).

Q2 — Wall-clock duration measurement. Three candidate sources: (a) compute from agent's own report timestamps (start_at vs end_at fields — most agents already write `ts` but not `started_at` + `ended_at`); (b) derive from scheduler's `lastRunAt` vs the next report file's mtime (lossy — might race with the next run); (c) instrument each agent's PRELUDE to capture `RUN_STARTED_AT=$(date -u +%FT%TZ)` and write to the final report. Recommend (c). Trivial to add. Five-minute change per prompt.

Q3 — Pricing table. Codify the per-million pricing for each model used in the pipeline: Opus 4.x ($X/M in, $Y/M out), Sonnet 4.x ($X/M in, $Y/M out), Haiku 4.x ($X/M in, $Y/M out). Cache pricing differs (cache-creation costs more than baseline input; cache-read costs less). Provide a small Node helper that takes `{input, output, cache_creation, cache_read, model}` and returns dollar cost. Store as `monitor/scripts/compute-run-cost.js` similar to compute-drift-audit.js.

Q4 — Variance / p95 tracking. For each Opus agent, compute median + p95 + max cost-per-run over the last 14 days from collected data. Flag agents where p95 > 3× median (signal of unbounded loops or rare-mode walks consuming far more than baseline). Today's Mode 3 walk vs a Mode 0 no-op should differ visibly here.

Q5 — Composite metric. The actual signal Mode 3 wants is `daily_cost = cost_per_run × runs_per_day × (1 - no_op_rate_for_substantive_cost)`. Agents that run frequently AND have high per-run cost AND high substantive-output rate are the optimization targets. Agents that are cheap OR rarely run OR overwhelmingly no-op are not. Rank agents by daily_cost and surface top-3.

Q6 — Keep static line-count tracking. The existing context_load section catches prompt drift (an agent's prompt grew by 50 lines without authorization) — a different failure mode from per-run variance. Both belong in the report. Don't replace; augment.

Q7 — Operator-Claude session cost (today's OBE audit, the PROP-100 author-and-implement). OUT OF SCOPE for this directive (scheduled-agent instrumentation), but tinker should NOTE in the PROP that this is the bigger blind spot and a Phase 2 follow-up if Phase 1 lands cleanly. Phase 2 would require operator-session JSONL aggregation, which raises privacy/scope questions out of band.

Q8 — Action threshold. Once cost is measured, what's the trigger for authoring a new optimization PROP? Today's report listed two standing candidates (decider dispatcher-split, workspace-sync script-extraction) and didn't act. Propose a numeric threshold: e.g., 'any Opus agent with daily_cost > $X/day AND no implemented optimization PROP for that agent in the last 30d → author PROP this run'. The threshold must be calibrated so today's pipeline state (let's say ~$Z/day total) triggers exactly ONE action item — not zero, not five.
deliverable: A PROP-NNN proposal in monitor/tinker/proposals/ with: (1) Q1 access-path mapping (with evidence of probe results); (2) Q2/Q3 instrumentation design — concrete bash for PRELUDE start-marker capture, concrete Node for cost computation; (3) Q4/Q5 variance + composite metric design with example output; (4) Q6 line-count co-existence; (5) Q7 noted as Phase 2; (6) Q8 threshold proposed; (7) one immediate test-run: have the PROP include the script to compute cost for tinker's OWN runs from the last 7 days as the first validation. Propose-only; operator integrates after review.
constraints: Honor the other-side: if Q1 finds tinker CANNOT access JSONL for other agents, the recommended fix is agent-side self-report (write `usage` field to existing report-*.json) — NOT a hack to grant tinker cross-session file access. Self-report is operator-style, additive, low-blast-radius.
Do NOT delete or weaken the existing context_load static-line-count tracking. It catches prompt-drift, a separate failure mode that real per-run measurement does not catch.

Do NOT design a Phase 1 that requires every agent's prompt to change. Phase 1 should be 'tinker computes costs from whatever data is currently available'; agent-side instrumentation (writing `usage` to report-*.json) is Phase 2 if Phase 1's data source is insufficient.

Other-side: measurement that's not actionable is waste. The PROP must answer: 'when this measurement says X, tinker does Y'. If Y is just 'add to standing-candidates list' indefinitely, then we haven't actually changed anything from today's state. Q8's threshold rule is the action commitment.

Honor: cache-read pricing matters. Modern Claude billing uses prompt-caching extensively; cache_read_input_tokens cost ~1/10th of regular input tokens. The cost helper MUST handle this correctly or the absolute dollar figures will be wrong by ~3-5×.
